name: KernelCAD
description: Agent-first CAD runtime for creating and reviewing 3D parts via editable TypeScript source files and OpenCASCADE kernel.

tools.name: review_paint_peek_latest
tools.title: Get Latest Painted Review Feedback
tools.description: Return the newest brush-painted review packet from a Studio session. After sharing a /p/<slug> link, the user can open it in the browser and paint marks over the 3D viewport to give visual feedback. Call this tool with the `slug` from that link to see the strokes â screenshot + mask + struck part names plus an optional one-line note and intent tags (e.g. "too thick", "missing", "wrong angle") describing WHAT is wrong â and act on the feedback. The slug is the capability: no OAuth required when passing `slug`; private projects require the owner to be signed in. Omit `slug` to fetch your own latest packet from your signed-in account (requires OAuth). By default returns short-lived signed Storage URLs for the screenshot + mask + meta.json plus the struck part names â small and context-friendly. Pass `paths_only: false` to also base64-inline the PNGs for clients that cannot fetch the signed URLs over HTTP.

slug.description: Project slug from open_in_studio/get_project/a /p/<slug> link. When given, returns the latest brush packet painted on that project's page â works without OAuth; the slug is the capability. Omit to use your signed-in account's latest packet.

freshness_sec.description: Maximum packet age in seconds. Default 1800 (30 min). Use a smaller value for "what did I just paint" or a larger one for "earlier today".

paths_only.description: Controls PNG delivery. Default (omitted or true): return only signed URLs + struck part names â the small, context-friendly response; fetch the bytes via the signed URLs. Set false to also base64-inline the screenshot + mask PNGs for clients that cannot fetch the URLs over HTTP (larger response).

tools.name: open_in_studio
tools.title: Open in Studio
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to SEE or share the model â it persists the current kernelCAD model and returns a one-click link that opens it in the kernelCAD Studio web app, where the user can view and share it. Pass the full `.kcad` source you have been building as `code`. `code` is OPTIONAL: if you just called `evaluate_script` you can omit it and this reuses that last evaluated source automatically (no need to re-send the whole script). Pass `code` explicitly to override, or whenever you have not evaluated this exact source yet. The result includes a `slug` â pass that `slug` on every subsequent call to UPDATE the same project in place: the user's open Studio tab re-renders live, so they can watch the model evolve as you iterate. Omit `slug` only for a new, separate model (each omission creates a new project and link). Trigger phrases: "open it in Studio", "let me see it", "show me the model"; also call it after you finish a build, and after each meaningful revision while iterating.

code.description: The full .kcad source of the model to open in Studio (the script you have been editing). Optional: omit to reuse the source from your most recent evaluate_script call.

title.description: Optional human-readable title for the model (shown in Studio). Defaults to "Model from Claude".

parameters.description: Optional list of the model's editable parameters, so Studio can render parameter controls. Each item is one control derived from the .kcad params.

name.description: Parameter identifier as used in the script (e.g. "width").

defaultValue.description: Current/default value of the parameter; type matches `kind`.

kind.description: Control type Studio should render for this parameter.

unit.description: Optional unit label shown next to the control (e.g. "mm", "deg").

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the parameter.

slug.description: Slug returned by a previous open_in_studio call. When given, updates that existing project in place (live-updating the user's open Studio tab) instead of creating a new one.

attachments.description: Complementary project files referenced by relative path from the .kcad source.

ok.description: Whether the model was persisted.

url.description: The /p/<slug> Studio link for the model.

embedUrl.description: Read-only, chrome-free /embed/<slug> viewer URL â drop into an <iframe> to embed the live model in any site or widget (no login).

slug.description: The project slug; pass it back to update this project in place.

version.description: Immutable Studio revision persisted by this call. Read it with get_project_revision using this slug and version.

updated.description: True when an existing project was updated; false when a new one was created.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get Project
tools.description: Use this when you need to reopen a saved project or browse what the user has saved â it fetches a kernelCAD Studio project, or lists the signed-in user's saved projects. Pass `slug` (from a /p/<slug> link or a prior listing) to fetch that project's full .kcad source and metadata â then edit and open_in_studio with the same slug so the user's open tab updates live. Private projects require their owner's OAuth connection. OMIT `slug` to list the signed-in user's saved projects (most recently updated first); that listing mode requires the OAuth connection.

slug.description: The project slug from a listing or a /p/<slug> Studio link. Omit to list the signed-in user's saved projects.

ok.description: Whether the read succeeded.

parameters.description: Fetch mode: the model's editable parameters.

assets.description: Complementary files keyed by source-relative path.

projects.description: List mode (no slug): the user's saved projects.

tools.name: get_project_revision
tools.title: Get Project Revision
tools.description: Fetch the exact immutable .kcad source and parameters captured at a prior `open_in_studio` version. Use this to read-after-write verify a release: pass the returned `slug` and `version`, then hash or inspect the returned source. Public/unlisted projects use the slug as capability; private projects require the owner's OAuth connection.

version.description: Positive immutable revision version returned by open_in_studio.

ok.description: Whether the revision was found and readable.

code.description: Exact .kcad source captured at this revision.

parameters.description: Exact editable parameters captured at this revision.

tools.name: get_latest_render
tools.title: Get Latest Render
tools.description: Render a project's current model server-side and return it as an inline image so you can SEE what you built. Use this after open_in_studio (or any /p/<slug> link): call with that `slug` to inspect whether the build looks right. CRITICAL â the image is rendered from the MODEL on the server; it does NOT reflect the user's Studio camera, zoom, or screen. NEVER ask the user to rotate, zoom, pan, move the camera, close a slider, or change their view to help you see â you cannot affect their screen and it cannot affect this render. To see a different angle, call this tool again with a different `view`. By DEFAULT (omit `view`, or `view:"all"`) it returns a CONTACT SHEET of all six canonical views in one labeled image â a 3Ã2 grid, top row [iso, front, right], bottom row [back, left, top] â so you can judge the model from every side regardless of its orientation (e.g. to find which side has the doors). Pass a single `view` (iso/front/back/left/right/top) for one large render of that angle. DETERMINISTIC: the same model + view always returns the same bytes â identical bytes are NOT a stale/lagging snapshot. If you changed the model, push it with open_in_studio FIRST, then re-render to see the change. The image is always current and never a blank capture. Colors and shading match Studio (same palette / base-material color). The slug is the capability: no OAuth for public/unlisted; private projects require the owner signed in. The PNG is base64-inlined as a real image block by default; pass `paths_only: true` for metadata only. No renderable geometry or a mesh failure â { ok: false, error, hint }, never a blank image.

slug.description: Project slug from open_in_studio/get_project/a /p/<slug> link. The slug is the capability â public/unlisted projects need no OAuth; private projects require the owner to be signed in.

view.description: View to render. Default "all" = a labeled contact sheet of every canonical angle (iso/front/back/left/right/top) â best for judging the whole model. Pass a single view name for one large render of that angle.

paths_only.description: Controls PNG delivery. Default false: base64-inline the rendered PNG so clients that cannot fetch a URL over HTTP (e.g. a sandboxed agent) can still see it. Set true to return only metadata (smaller response).

ok.description: Whether a render was produced.

image_b64.description: Base64-encoded PNG bytes, present when inlined (paths_only=false) and under the size cap.

truncated.description: Set when inline was requested but the PNG exceeded the size cap.

view.description: The view that was rendered (when ok).

width.description: Rendered image edge in px (when ok).

height.description: Rendered image edge in px (when ok).

error.description: Error code when ok is false (e.g. "empty_geometry", "mesh_failed").

hint.description: Next-action hint when ok is false.

tools.name: get_model_mesh
tools.title: Get Model Mesh
tools.description: Return the raw per-feature triangle mesh (positions/indices/normals) of a project's current model, by slug. For the in-chat 3D viewer widget to render geometry; delivered over the MCP Apps bridge. The slug is the capability: public/unlisted need no OAuth; private requires the owner signed in.

tools.name: lookup_authoring_skill
tools.title: Look Up Authoring Skill
tools.description:
Return the kernelcad-authoring SKILL.md body â conventions for writing .kcad.ts scripts (imports, parameters, evaluation contract, common pitfalls).

Use this tool BEFORE generating CAD code if your MCP client does not list resources. Clients that do list resources should instead read `kernelcad://skills/authoring` directly â the contents are identical.

INPUT: none. OUTPUT: { uri, mimeType, text } where `text` is the SKILL.md body.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the returned body.

tools.name: mesh_summary
tools.title: Summarize Mesh Geometry
tools.description:
Mesh a kernelCAD .kcad.ts source server-side and return a COMPACT geometry summary â overall bounds plus, per feature, its id, kind, triangle count, and bounding box.

Use this to INSPECT a model's geometry without a viewer: confirm a part is the size/shape you expect, see how many triangles each feature contributes, or check that every feature produced geometry. This runs the full server-side OCCT pipeline (the same one the Studio renderer uses), so it evaluates modern sources (assembly, path, .material, â¦) that the legacy client worker cannot.

INPUT: `source` (required) the .kcad.ts script text; `fileName` (optional) a label for diagnostics; `params` (optional) a map of parameter-name â number overrides applied before meshing (stateless slider recompute).

OUTPUT: { ok, bounds, featureCount, features: [{ id, kind, triangleCount, bbox: { min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z] } }], failedFeatureIds, diagnostics }. `ok` is true when every feature meshed; `failedFeatureIds` lists features that failed to compile (and `ok` is then false). Raw vertex/index/normal arrays are NEVER returned â this is a summary only. To SEE the rendered model, use open_in_studio + get_latest_render instead.

fileName.description: Optional file-name label used in diagnostics (does not affect geometry).

params.description: Optional map of parameter-name â numeric value, applied as overrides before meshing (stateless slider recompute).

ok.description: True when every feature meshed successfully.

featureCount.description: Number of features in the meshed model.

features.description: Per-feature summary â never includes raw mesh arrays.

failedFeatureIds.description: Feature ids that failed to compile (empty when ok).

tools.name: evaluate_script
tools.title: Evaluate CAD Script
tools.description: Use this when you need to run a script and check it compiles. Run a kernelCAD .kcad.ts script and report pass/fail + feature count + diagnostics. When the scene is assembly-built (assembly().part(...) â .model()/.solvedModel()), also returns a parts summary { count, names }. Pass either { file: "<path>" } or { code: "<inline source>" }. Set { dryRun: true } for fast validation while iterating: transpile + capture + capture-light checks WITHOUT OCCT lowering, DFM gates, or meshing â milliseconds instead of seconds (100x+ on boolean/fillet-heavy scripts). A dry run catches script throws, capture-time API misuse, and assembly validity-gate failures, but NOT lowering failures or dfmSpec diagnostics; it leaves the active session untouched, so finish with a full (non-dry) evaluate_script before using session-dependent tools.

dryRun.description: Fast validation only: skip OCCT lowering, DFM gates, and meshing. Does not set or clear the active session.

ok.description: Whether the script compiled and lowered cleanly.

featureCount.description: Number of features captured by the script.

dryRun.description: True when the result came from a fast dry run.

parts.description: Assembly parts summary { count, names } when the scene is assembly-built.

tools.name: diff_scripts
tools.title: Diff CAD Scripts
tools.description: Use this when you need to see exactly what changed between two script versions. Structured geometric delta between two versions of a kernelCAD script â a baseline ({ baseFile } or { baseCode }) and a revision ({ file } or { code }). Returns agent-readable JSON: per-part added/removed/renamed/changed (volume mmÂ³ + exact bbox deltas, numbers matching inspect({ of: 'part-stats' })), total interference-volume delta with per-pair detail, mate-graph changes (added/removed/changed mates incl. type, connectors, pose, limits), and param changes (value/min/max). Single-shape scripts diff as one "(root)" pseudo-part. Use after editing a script to verify exactly what changed physically before re-rendering. Read-only â never touches the active session.

baseFile.description: Baseline script â path to a .kcad.ts file.

file.description: Revised script â path to a .kcad.ts file.

tools.name: inspect
tools.title: Inspect Model
tools.description:
Use this when you need to read facts about a model. One reader, selected by `of`:
- 'assembly' â physical assembly inventory (parts, bboxes, connectors, mates, disconnected solids).
- 'robot' â URDF/SDFormat export preview (links, joints, planning groups, end-effectors, issues).
- 'step' â inspect an imported STEP file.
- 'shape' â volume / surfaceArea / bbox for one feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'features' â features captured by the script (kind, id, params, transforms, suppression).
- 'assemblies' â assembly intent (assemblies, parts, connectors, joints).
- 'topology' â canonical face names + edge count for a feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'edges' â edges of a shape with optional EdgeQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-edges' â boundary edges of a named canonical face ({ feature_id?, face_name }).
- 'faces' â faces of a shape with optional FaceQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-labels' â user-applied labels visible in the script.
- 'mates' â mates captured by the script.
- 'constraints' â sketch constraints captured by the script.
- 'part-stats' â bundled parts-catalog statistics.
- 'bend-table' â sheet-metal bend table for a flattened pattern.
- 'params' â declared model parameters.
- 'part-categories' â top-level part-catalog categories available in the bundled (and configured remote) catalog.
- 'part-families' â part families within a category ({ category? }); count + exemplar ids per family.
All params except `of` are subject-specific and forwarded verbatim. Most subjects accept { file | code }.

assembly.description: of:'assembly'|'robot' â assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

feature_id.description: of:'shape'|'topology'|'edges'|'faces'|'face-edges'|'face-labels' â FeatureId; defaults to the last returned shape.

face_name.description: of:'face-edges' â canonical face name (required for that subject).

category.description: of:'part-families' â optional top-level category to filter families by.

ok.description: Whether the read succeeded.

tools.name: verify
tools.title: Verify Design
tools.description:
Use this when you need to check a design against a rule set. One verifier, selected by `check`:
- 'assembly' â mate-aware assembly validator on the active session (run evaluate_script first).
- 'urdf' â structural validity of a .urdf file ({ urdf_path }).
- 'dfm' â print-readiness gates declared by dfmSpec() ({ file | code }).
- 'dfm-preflight' â sheet-metal flat pattern vs a job-shop's ordering rules ({ vendor, material, thicknessIn|thicknessMm, ... }).
- 'swept-collision' â sweep declared joint range(s) and report colliding poses.
- 'reachable' â inverse-kinematics reachability for an end-effector ({ tip_link, target_position, ... }).
- 'mounting-holes' â fastened mates expose matching hole diameters on both sides.
- 'load-capacity' â closed-form Euler-Bernoulli beam stress / safety-factor check ({ loads, materials, ... }).
All params except `check` are check-specific and forwarded verbatim; each check fails closed on its own missing required params.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source (same checks as `file`).

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

urdf_path.description: check:'urdf' â path to the .urdf file.

dxf.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â path to a DXF file.

featureId.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â FeatureId to scope to.

vendor.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â vendor SKU (required for that check).

material.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â material SKU (required for that check).

thicknessIn.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â material thickness in inches.

thicknessMm.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â material thickness in millimeters.

refreshCatalog.description: check:'dfm-preflight' â force vendor catalog refresh.

joint.description: check:'swept-collision' â joint to sweep; omit to sweep every declared joint.

range.description: check:'swept-collision' â [lower, upper, step] in joint-native units.

collision_tolerance_mm3.description: check:'swept-collision' â BREP intersection volume tolerance (mm^3).

tip_link.description: check:'reachable' â end-effector part name (required for that check).

target_position.description: check:'reachable' â target [x, y, z] mm (world frame).

target_orientation.description: check:'reachable' â target XYZ Euler angles in radians.

position_tolerance_mm.description: check:'reachable' â position tolerance in mm.

orientation_tolerance_rad.description: check:'reachable' â orientation tolerance in radians.

prefer_solver.description: check:'reachable' â force the IK path ('auto' default).

seed.description: check:'reachable' â numeric IK seed pose (joint name -> deg/mm).

loads.description: check:'load-capacity' â partName -> { force?: [Fx,Fy,Fz] N, torque?: [Tx,Ty,Tz] N*m }.

ok.description: Whether the verification ran and passed its gate.

tools.name: why_did_this_fail
tools.title: Explain Failure
tools.description: Use this when you need to trace why a feature failed. Walk the upstream chain of a failing feature. Returns the diagnostics of the requested feature plus the diagnostics of every upstream feature in topological order (the requested feature is the last entry). Per-code hints are inline on every diagnostic â call lookup_diagnostics for the full catalogue. Pass { file?, code?, feature_id? }.

chain.description: Upstream feature diagnostics in topological order; requested feature last.

tools.name: set_param
tools.title: Set Parameter
tools.description: Use this when you need to edit a param() default value in a kernelCAD script. Returns the modified code as text plus diagnostics from re-evaluating the result. Caller persists the new code via standard file-write tools (this tool has no side effects).

param_name.description: The string literal name of the param (first arg to param()).

new_value.description: The new default value. Either a number for a numeric param (e.g. 12.5), or a string expression evaluated in the script (e.g. "width/2 + 3").

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

binding_name.description: JS const name bound to the new construct (when one was created).

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics from re-evaluating the modified source.

error.description: Failure message (present when ok is false).

tools.name: add_feature
tools.title: Add Feature
tools.description: Use this when you need to insert a new feature line into a script. Insert a new feature line into a kernelCAD script before the last top-level return statement. Returns the modified code as text plus diagnostics from re-evaluating the result. Side-effect-free. Primitives that accept faceLabels (box, cylinder, extrudeRect, extrudeCircle, extrudePolygon, extrudeRoundedRect) can receive `opts.faceLabels` in the inserted code â use `lookup_api` to see `featureKindFaceLabels` for the full value schema.

feature_code.description: Single-statement source line to insert (e.g. `const hole = cylinder(5, 2).translate(10, 10, -1);`).

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

binding_name.description: JS const name bound to the new construct (when one was created).

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics from re-evaluating the modified source.

error.description: Failure message (present when ok is false).

tools.name: add_surface
tools.title: Add Surface
tools.description:
Use this when you need to author a NURBS Surface into the user's .kcad.ts. One authoring path, selected by `kind`:
- 'nurbs' â insert a nurbsSurface(...) / surfaceFromCurves(...) call. Pass either { controls, degree, weights?, knots?, periodic? } for direct construction, OR { section_sketch_ids } for skinning. Slice-1 limitation: weights are accepted but currently ignored (TColStd_Array2OfReal not exposed in WASM bindings); surfaces are non-rational.
- 'boundary' â insert a surfaceFromBoundary([c1,c2,c3,c4], opts?) call: one NURBS face through 4 boundary Curve3D refs (bottom, right, top, left in loop order; adjacent endpoints must coincide within 1e-6 mm) via OCCT BRepOffsetAPI_MakeFilling.
The returned Surface produces no Shape until you chain .thicken(t) or .toShape() (do that via add_feature on the binding name). Returns the modified code + diagnostics. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

controls.description: kind:'nurbs' â control-point grid for direct construction (controls[u][v] = [x, y, z], mm).

weights.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional rational weights, same grid shape as controls. Ignored in slice-1.

degree.description: kind:'nurbs' â degrees in U and V; each in [1, nU-1] / [1, nV-1].

knots.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional explicit knot vectors; missing => clamped uniform inferred.

periodic.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional periodic flags per parametric direction.

section_sketch_ids.description: kind:'nurbs' â existing sketch FeatureIds (2 or more) to skin a surface through, in order.

curve_bindings.description: kind:'boundary' â tuple of 4 existing Curve3D variable names (bottom, right, top, left) declared earlier in the source.

continuity.description: kind:'boundary' â continuity grade applied to every edge ('C0' | 'C1' | 'C2'), or an array of 4 grades (one per edge, bottom/right/top/left order). Default 'C0'.

sampling.description: kind:'boundary' â OCCT NbPtsOnCur sampling parameter (default 15).

binding_name.description: JS const name for the new Surface binding (kind:'nurbs' default surface_<N>; kind:'boundary' default _surface_<N>).

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

binding_name.description: JS const name bound to the new construct (when one was created).

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics from re-evaluating the modified source.

error.description: Failure message (present when ok is false).

tools.name: add_curve
tools.title: Add Curve
tools.description:
Use this when you need to author a 3D Curve3D into the user's .kcad.ts immediately before the last top-level return. One authoring path, selected by `kind`:
- 'nurbs' â insert a `nurbsCurve(controlPoints, opts?)` declaration. Pass `controlPoints` as a Vec3[] (mm, at least 2 points). Optional NURBS knobs: `degree` (default 3), rational `weights`, explicit `knots`, `closed`.
- 'hermite' â insert a `hermiteG2(a, b)` declaration: a quintic Hermite curve interpolating two endpoints with matching positions, tangents, and (optional) curvatures â bridges two curves with G2 continuity. Each endpoint is `{ point: Vec3, tangent: Vec3, curvature?: Vec3 }` in mm; tangent magnitude ~ chord length; curvature defaults to [0,0,0] (G1-only).
The returned binding has type Curve3D (peer to Shape / Surface) â consume it via `add_variable_sweep` (spine input), `add_surface({ kind: 'boundary' })` (boundary curve), or downstream Curve3D-accepting features. Returns the modified code + diagnostics from re-evaluating. Side-effect-free. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

controlPoints.description: kind:'nurbs' â control points as Vec3 triples in mm; at least 2 entries.

weights.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional rational weights, one per control point (same length as controlPoints).

knots.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional explicit knot vector; missing => clamped-uniform inferred.

tangent.description: First derivative of the curve at this endpoint.
First derivative of the curve at this endpoint.

binding_name.description: JS const name for the new Curve3D binding (default: _curve_<N>).

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

binding_name.description: JS const name bound to the new construct (when one was created).

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics from re-evaluating the modified source.

error.description: Failure message (present when ok is false).

tools.name: add_path_segment
tools.title: Add Path Segment
tools.description:
Use this when you need to append a curved segment to an existing PathBuilder chain on the named `chain_anchor` variable. The call is injected at the END of the chain, immediately before any `.close()`. One segment kind, selected by `kind`:
- 'spline' â `.spline(points, opts?)`: interpolates through every `points` waypoint (Vec2[] mm, >= 2 entries; points[0] must match current pen position). Optional `tension`, and `startTangent`/`endTangent` 2D direction vectors that constrain the first-derivative direction at the endpoints (magnitude normalised internally). Use for organic 2D outlines (eyewear brow, ergonomic handle, sneaker midsole).
- 'nurbs' â `.nurbsSegment(controlPoints, opts?)`: explicit B-spline net (Vec2[] mm, >= degree+1 entries; controlPoints[0] must match pen; pen ends at controlPoints[N-1]). Optional `degree` (default 3), rational `weights` (strictly positive), explicit `knots` (length = controlPoints.length + degree + 1).
- 'hermite' â `.hermiteG2(a, b)`: each endpoint `{ point: Vec2, tangent: Vec2, curvature?: Vec2 }` in mm (a.point must match pen; pen ends at b.point). `curvature` defaults to [0,0] (G1); pass matching curvatures for G2 blends. Tangent magnitude is the first derivative (~ chord length), NOT unit length.
Returns the modified code + diagnostics from re-evaluating. Side-effect-free. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

chain_anchor.description: JS identifier of an existing PathBuilder binding (e.g. `const brow = path().moveTo(0,0)`).

points.description: kind:'spline' â waypoints as Vec2 pairs in mm; at least 2 entries; first must match current pen position.

tension.description: kind:'spline' â optional Catmull-Rom-style stiffness; forwarded to the underlying B-spline approximation.

startTangent.description: kind:'spline' â optional [x, y] direction vector at points[0]. Magnitude is normalised internally; direction matters.

endTangent.description: kind:'spline' â optional [x, y] direction vector at points[N-1]. Magnitude is normalised internally; direction matters.

controlPoints.description: kind:'nurbs' â control-net vertices as Vec2 pairs in mm; at least degree+1 entries.

weights.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional rational weights (one per control point; strictly positive).

knots.description: kind:'nurbs' â optional explicit knot vector; length must equal controlPoints.length + degree + 1.

a.description: kind:'hermite' â start endpoint; point must match current pen position within 1e-6 mm.

tangent.description: First derivative (~ chord length), NOT unit length.

b.description: kind:'hermite' â end endpoint; pen ends at b.point.

tangent.description: First derivative (~ chord length), NOT unit length.

binding_name.description: Reserved for future use; the segment injection mutates the chain anchor in place.

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

tools.name: trace_from_image
tools.title: Trace Outline from Image
tools.description: Use this when you need to trace features from a reference photo into waypoints. Trace pixel-space features from a reference photo into normalized [0..1] waypoints the agent can map to mm via a known scale anchor and feed to path().spline / path().nurbsSegment. Three backends are dispatched behind the scenes: `opencv` (deterministic; uniform-bg silhouette only), `vision-llm` (Claude vision; named points/cluttered backgrounds; caller-supplied ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), and `hybrid` (opencv silhouette + LLM-labeled named points). Default backend is `auto` â the tool picks based on the image's corner-color stddev. Accuracy honesty: opencv contour is geometrically exact; vision-LLM is typically 5â10% off on dense landmarks. Per-feature `confidence` is reported. Caller pays for any vision-LLM API spend via their own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Pair with the `kernelcad-trace-from-image` skill for the conversion-to-mm pipeline.

imageUrl.description: URL or path to the reference image. Supports file://, http(s)://, data:image/...;base64,..., or a bare filesystem path.

hint.description: Optional free-text hint forwarded to vision-LLM backends (e.g. "a pair of eyewear; trace the upper brow only").

features.description: Features to trace. Defaults to a single { label: "silhouette", kind: "silhouette" } when omitted.

kind.description: Geometric shape of the requested feature.

region.description: Optional free-text region hint forwarded to vision-LLM backends; ignored by opencv.

maxWaypointsPerFeature.description: Cap on waypoints per feature. Defaults to 12 (suitable for medium-inflection outlines).

backend.description: Force a specific backend; default `auto` routes by corner-color stddev.

features.description: Traced features with normalized [0..1] waypoints + confidence.

imageDims.description: Pixel dimensions [width, height] of the source image.

tools.name: add_variable_sweep

tools.description: Use this when you need to author a variable-section sweep along a spine. Insert a `variableSweep(spine, sections, opts?)` declaration into the user's .kcad.ts immediately before the last top-level return. The result is a Shape â chain `.translate(...)`, `.union(...)`, etc. via `add_feature`. `spine_binding` references an existing variable (Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[]) in the source; each `sections[i].profile_binding` references an existing Sketch. Sections must be strictly increasing in `t` and span [0, 1]; first t=0, last t=1. Orientation is not exposed by this MCP tool until runtime orientation support is wired. Validates every binding exists in the source via regex before inserting (fast structured error vs capture-time stack). Returns the modified code + diagnostics. Side-effect-free.

tools.name: add_text
tools.title: Add Text
tools.description:
Use this when you need to author text into a kernelCAD script before the last top-level return. One authoring path, selected by `mode`:
- 'sketch' â insert a sketch.text(...) call. The emitted sketch is chainable: pair with subsequent .extrude(...) / cut(...) edits to land an engraved or raised text feature.
- 'emboss' â insert a `<shape>.embossText({...})` chained call onto an existing Shape `target`. Use for engraved brand text on faces (Ray-Ban temple, CE mark, model number). `depth > 0` raises text out of the face; `depth < 0` engraves text into the face. Lowers via replicad drawText â sketchOnFace â extrude â fuse|cut.
Default font is the runtime-bundled Liberation Sans. Side-effect-free; returns the modified code plus diagnostics from re-evaluating. Each mode fails closed on its own missing required params.

font.description: mode:'sketch' â optional logical font name or .ttf file path; defaults to bundled Liberation Sans.

align.description: mode:'sketch' â horizontal alignment relative to position (default left); mode:'emboss' â relative to the UV anchor (default center).

position.description: mode:'sketch' â [x, y] anchor in mm. Default [0, 0].

rotation.description: mode:'sketch' â CCW rotation in degrees around position (default 0); mode:'emboss' â CCW rotation in the face tangent plane (default 0).

bindAs.description: mode:'sketch' â emits `const <bindAs> = sketch.text(...)`; mode:'emboss' â emits `const <bindAs> = <target>.embossText(...);`.

tools.name: export
tools.title: Export
tools.description:
Use this when you need to export geometry to a file. One exporter, selected by `target`:
- target:'model' â export the script geometry to one file. Pass { file | code }, a required { output_path }, and { format }. Supported formats: stl (binary STL mesh), step (BREP CAD interchange), dxf (planar laser/waterjet profile from a Region or planar face), 3mf (slicer-friendly mesh with per-part colors), glb (web-viewer / AR with PBR materials), svg-drawing (third-angle engineering-drawing sheet: front/top/left + isometric views, hidden edges dashed, tangent edges thin, overall bounding-box dimensions, title block; assemblies are drawn with inter-part occlusion). Robot descriptions: urdf (tree-topology robot description), srdf (motion-planning semantics layered over the URDF), sdf-gazebo (SDFormat 1.10 with native ball joints, closed loops, and solved per-link poses). urdf and sdf-gazebo also write one meshes/<part>.stl per link next to output_path (reported in mesh_files) â ship the whole directory to the consumer. STL exports run a watertight verify by default; failures return ok: false with export.mesh.not-watertight (open-edge count + up to 5 crack-cluster locations) but the file is still written so the broken mesh can be inspected. Optional { feature_id } selects which feature to export (default: last). Optional { options } carries per-format options bag (see the kernelcad-mcp skill for the per-format keys: dxf layers/tolerance/unit, 3mf printUnit/embedSource, glb axis/draco).
- target:'part' â export solved-assembly parts as individual binary STL files in their modeled (world-frame) positions. Pass { file | code }, plus { part, output_path } for one part or { output_dir } for all parts (files land at <output_dir>/<part>.stl). A watertight verify runs on every exported mesh by default and fails the call with export.mesh.not-watertight; unknown part names fail with export.part.not-found listing the valid names.
Pass { no_verify: true } to skip the watertight gate. All params except `target` are forwarded verbatim; each target fails closed on its own missing required params.

target.description: Which exporter to run: 'model' (whole-script geometry to one file) or 'part' (per-part STLs from a solved assembly).

output_path.description: Destination path. target:'model' â the export file (required). target:'part' â single-part .stl path.

format.description: target:'model' â output file format (required for that target).

feature_id.description: target:'model' â optional FeatureId to export; defaults to last.

options.description: target:'model' â optional per-format options bag. Discriminator options.format must equal top-level format. dxf: { layers?, unit?: "mm"|"cm"|"in", tolerance? }. 3mf: { printUnit?: "mm"|"cm"|"in", embedSource? }. glb: { axis?: "y-up"|"z-up", draco?: false }. svg-drawing: { sheet?: "a4"|"a3", modelName?, date? }.

part.description: target:'part' â part name for single-part export, or 'all'.

output_dir.description: target:'part' â destination directory (all-parts mode); files are <dir>/<part>.stl.

no_verify.description: Skip the STL watertight verify gate.

Fitness includes repairMode: none, local-fix, parameter-tune, or topology-redesign.

tools.title: Capture Animation
tools.description: Use this when you need to render a script's animation timeline to a video. Capture a kernelCAD script's animationView({...}) timeline to an MP4 (ffmpeg) or a PNG frame sequence, verifying the sampled poses for part interference. FILE ONLY: pass { file } (a .kcad.ts path) â there is no { code } mode, because the capture engine renders from a file on disk (its relative lib.fromSTEP imports resolve against the script directory). MP4 by default; pass { frames_dir } to write frame-0000.png... and skip ffmpeg entirely (mutually exclusive with output_path). Animation-pose interference verification runs by default (keyframe times + segment midpoints) BEFORE any browser/ffmpeg cost; { no_verify: true } skips it and { verify_every: n } additionally samples every n-th frame time. Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts in the rendered frames â same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`; visibility is render-only and does NOT affect the pose verification. Collisions DO NOT fail the call â the artifact is still written as evidence with ok: true; read verified: false + the collisions[] array. ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENT (identical to `kernelcad render`): capture drives a headless browser against a running studio dev server reachable at http://localhost:5173 (or the VITE_PORT override); there is no bundled-static serving mode yet, so the same dev-server precondition applies in a production MCP install. Returns { ok, output_path, frame_count, duration_ms, fps, verified, verify_skipped?, collisions: [{ t_ms, a, b, volume_mm3 }], diagnostics }.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script with an animationView({...}) record. Required (no inline { code } mode).

output_path.description: MP4 output path; default <scriptDir>/<basename>-animation.mp4. Mutually exclusive with frames_dir.

frames_dir.description: PNG-sequence mode directory: write frame-0000.png... and skip ffmpeg. Mutually exclusive with output_path.

no_verify.description: Skip the animation-pose interference verification (default: verify on).

verify_every.description: Additionally verify at every n-th frame time of the fps schedule (unioned with the keyframe sample set).

focus.description: Show only matching feature ids / assembly part names in the rendered frames. Mutually exclusive with hide. Render-only; does not affect pose verification.

hide.description: Hide matching feature ids / assembly part names in the rendered frames. Mutually exclusive with focus. Render-only; does not affect pose verification.

collisions.description: Colliding poses { t_ms, a, b, volume_mm3 }.

tools.name: render_preview
tools.title: Render Preview
tools.description: Use this when you need to LOOK at a kernelCAD model â render its script to deterministic PNG views for visual self-check (the visual half of the evaluate â render â inspect â fix loop), with NO studio or dev server required. Pass { code } (inline source) or { file } (a .kcad.ts path), exactly one. Renders the canonical engineering views (front, right, top, iso â pass { views } for a subset, e.g. ["iso"] for fastest iteration) plus an optional { pose: "<az>,<el>" } arbitrary camera angle (degrees; az=0,el=0 is front, +az rotates CCW around +Z, +el lifts the camera). NO STUDIO / DEV-SERVER REQUIRED: a prebuilt static player (dist/headless-player) is served from an ephemeral local port automatically; a running studio dev server is used as fallback, and { base_url } forces one. The only environment dependency is playwright chromium (npx playwright install chromium). Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts â same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`. PNGs are written to { out_dir } (default: a fresh temp session directory) and returned as absolute paths with per-view camera descriptions (kernelCAD is Z-up). Mechanism truth runs first, same protocol as `kernelcad render`: a broken mechanism still renders but every tile is watermarked MECHANISM BROKEN (KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1 refuses instead); read { mechanism, mechanism_failure_codes }. The probe runs full BREP interference sweeps and can dominate latency on large assemblies â pass { no_mechanism_check: true } for fast iteration (the preview then reports mechanism: "unverified"; ignored under strict mode). Returns { ok, images: [{ name, path, description }], out_dir, bounds, mechanism, render_source, render_ms, diagnostics }. PATHS ARE LOCAL to the machine running the MCP server â local stdio clients read them directly; hosted/remote clients should use open_in_studio instead.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source. Mutually exclusive with file. Relative imports resolve against a temp dir â use file for scripts with relative lib.fromSTEP(...) imports.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script on disk. Mutually exclusive with code.

views.description: Canonical views to render as an array, e.g. ["iso"] or ["front","top"] (default: all four). Fewer views = faster.

pose.description: Extra arbitrary camera pose '<az>,<el>' in degrees, e.g. '30,20'.

focus.description: Show only matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with hide.

hide.description: Hide matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with focus.

out_dir.description: Directory for the PNGs (created if missing). Default: a fresh temp session dir.

environment.description: HDRI environment override: preset ('studio', 'softbox', 'neutral', 'outdoor', 'warehouse'), a URL, or 'none' for the default three-light rig.

no_mechanism_check.description: Skip the mechanism-truth probe for fast iteration on large assemblies; the preview reports mechanism: 'unverified'. Ignored under KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1.

base_url.description: Advanced: force a specific render server (e.g. a running studio dev server) instead of the bundled static player.

ok.description: Whether the preview rendered.

images.description: Rendered tiles { name, path, description } â absolute local PNG paths with per-view camera orientation (kernelCAD is Z-up).

out_dir.description: Directory holding the PNGs (session temp dir unless out_dir was given).

bounds.description: Model AABB in mm { min, max } the camera was fit to (success).

mechanism_failure_codes.description: De-duplicated failure codes when mechanism is 'broken'.

render_ms.description: Wall-clock render time in ms (provisioning + browser + captures).
